title: Pressure cookers cook by letting water get hotter
body: Sealed steam raises the pressure inside a cooker to roughly an extra atmosphere, lifting water's boiling point from 100 to about 120 degrees Celsius. Cooking chemistry speeds up sharply with those twenty degrees, so beans soften in a third of the time. The invention is a thermostat hack played on the phase diagram.
source_hint: Phase diagram of water; Papin digester history (1679)
